target_customer: Pharma partners (for example GSK and Boehringer Ingelheim) that license liver targets and RNA therapies, and eventually patients with chronic liver disease
problem: Chronic liver diseases such as MASH fibrosis and cirrhosis have few treatments, and liver transplants are limited to about 40,000 a year versus 1.5 million deaths from liver disease per company figures.
business_model: Biotech drug developer: pipeline of RNA medicines plus pharma research collaborations with upfront and milestone payments
product_category: RNA therapeutics for liver disease, using human donor liver perfusion and genomics for target discovery

founders.name: Quin Wills
prior_employers: Novo Nordisk (established and led advanced genomics department)
education: Three further degrees in mathematics and computational biology from Cambridge and Oxford including a PhD in systems genomics
previous_startups: SimuGen (co-founded during PhD, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Background from the Gaingels profile. YC page lists him as Founder/CSO; the company site now lists him as Founder and CEO.

founders.name: Jack O'Meara
education: University of Galway (graduate, per Irish Times)
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO and co-founder in the June 2021 seed release and in the October 2022 Irish Times article. Not listed on the YC page, and the company site now lists Quin Wills as CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines multi-omics on perfused human donor livers, machine learning target discovery and GalNAc-siRNA design, a research-grade drug discovery stack.

defensibility.rationale: Access to human donor livers through transplant centre partners and proprietary datasets (over 20M USD invested in human liver data per the company) are hard to copy, but RNA drug classes themselves are not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pharma chose to partner instead: GSK research collaboration (reported 2024, moved to co-exclusive license in November 2025) and Boehringer Ingelheim in April 2024.

market_need_then: Liver disease affects millions with no approved regenerative or antifibrotic options for cirrhosis, and the 2021 seed release said deep phenotyping of discarded donor livers could find new targets.

branding.domain_note: Uses ochre-bio.com (hyphenated .com) per the company site.

identity.logo: Described by Bioescalator as a logo with a large white surrounding border; no further description
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led: Ochre exists to end the need for liver transplants

branding.brand_signature: Mission statement about ending the need for liver transplants

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage is about science and deals, not the brand; no source explains the name and no community evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Ochre Bio is active and grew to about 50 people. It raised a 9.6M seed in June 2021 led by Khosla, a 30M Series A in October 2022, and signed pharma deals with Boehringer Ingelheim (April 2024, 35M upfront and near-term, over 1B potential) and GSK. A science-heavy founder with genomics leadership at Novo Nordisk and a donor liver platform explains the credibility, while the drug pipeline remains preclinical or early.
notes: Series A announced 2022-10-10 per a Business Wire listing (page returned 403 when opened) and written up 2022-10-19 by the Irish Times; the 2022-10-19 date is from the opened article. Boehringer 35M is upfront and near-term fees, recorded as other and is partnership money, not equity. No dated competitor source found near the batch, so the list is empty. YC page lists only Quin Wills; Jack O'Meara is a co-founder per the seed release. Founding 2019 per YC page.
